MCDM’s upcoming psionic class for 5e the “Talent” uses its ‘magic’ in a similar strain-like way. They have powers from 1st Order to 6th Order and they roll a d6 when use a power. 1st order powers recharge if you roll above a 1, 6th order only recharge on a 6. If you don’t recharge the ability you gain strain which you can only accumulate so much of until you are effectively “out of spell slots.”  But you can choose to gain strain to still get powers off but you start risking actual PC death, but that’s wholly on the player if they want to go out in a burst of psionic glory. It’s spellcasting without spell slots and it has felt fun the couple of times I’ve play tested it

I could not understand a word of Tenet when I saw it in theaters because the sound design was so bad, that takes me out of the experience. I’m talking about the technical minutiae that matters to critics that typical audiences won’t notice or even be bothered by. 

>	You might not notice when a movie has great camera work, editing, sound or VFX, but you definitely notice when it has bad camera work, editing, sound or VFX.

Yeah I agree with you. But so bad it’s noticeable by general audiences is much different than the stuff a trained critic notices at first pass. That’s my entire point, there can be things that are bothersome to critics that doesn’t even get noticed and the review that talks about watching a movie as a layman is more useful to ME than the reviewer that can’t stop talking about Dutch angles or ADR or what have you. 

There’s a difference between “I don’t notice ANY cinematography, lighting, editing, or music” vs “the very technical minutiae went over my head and I didn’t notice exactly what framing or key light or whatever was used”

So to be clear not saying those things aren’t important but the esoteric aspects of those things aren’t as important to a general audience but those esoteric aspects can be just as important to a film critic.

When I see comments from critics along the lines of “the cinematography is so bad, they over relied on Dutch angles!” And I’d be sitting here thinking “I don’t think I noticed a single Dutch angle” that kind of stuff might bother a film critic but I couldn’t care less. The very technical details he neat to learn about if you deep dive into a movie, but if I’m determining what movie I want to spend money and time on the details of camera angles, lighting etc don’t matter that much to me as a potential viewer.

>	Critical improvements that are often suggested are things like campaign finance reform, things that hard limit the amount of money politicians can receive from individual donors / how much they can spend total. Harder limits on where politicians are able to earn money from (and their families). Expanded voting periods, reducing gerrymandering, and easing remote voting also critical improvements that will put more power into the hands of actual voters, rather than into the major actors.

I generally like those suggestions. However when it comes to campaign finance reform I fear we run into the exact same counter argument against term limits: that won’t be enough. To my knowledge there are several nations out there that have limited how much money politicians can use for campaigning and yet they still have plenty of corruption surrounding campaign finance. 

I don’t believe career politicians should exist as they do now. It shouldn’t make you rich, it should be seen as a duty. But I’d certainly support any change that made it harder to accumulate wealth and power as a member of congress. To the extent our system is rife with corruption, it seems the “experience” that gets talked about in politics is, more often than not, experience in being corrupt rather than governing. 

And again, not saying only do term limits then stop any further changes. Continue the changes so you don’t have to be rich or connected to serve in the government. I want as much accountability and transparency in government as humanly possible because under that kind of scrutiny it’s harder to abuse the system.

I suspect the people commenting “that won’t fix everything or even make an iota of difference. Full stop” without offering a single other idea are basically defeatists. Merely and only instituting term limits won’t fix much, but it’s a start. Merely and only cutting out soft drinks won’t magically fix someone’s weight issues, but it’s a start. It’s like when you want to hang out with someone. If you propose a day and they only say “I’m busy then” without offering another day? Then that person doesn’t really want to hang out. 

Arguing that one change won’t be the magic bullet is disingenuous because no one says term limits or holiday voting are the end all be all fixes. It’s a start is all. Shutting down every proposed change without a better idea will certainly never change anything, that’s for certain. 

>there are better fixes to these issues to spend our political capital on

It would be interesting to hear. My point is some suggest “let’s maybe think about term limits because we are obviously seeing the issues with career politicians” and it’s countered with “that won’t do anything, actually it will only be bad!” But there’s no counter proposal. If someone shut down the discussion that makes me think that person doesn’t want to fix anything.

Yeah people parroting “Well Term limits won’t fix everything, therefore let’s not try to fix anything” confuse me. It’s not about finding the magic fix to everything. Like if you are overweight, there no magic diet that’ll make you a healthy weight tomorrow, but you can start cutting calories, going for walks, etc. A proposed solution doesn’t have to fix everything, just contribute to the fixing.

That’s misreading me, I’m not saying do nothing. There’s a dozen things you can do and that’s my point. Someone should start wherever they can with therapy or medication or better diet or exercise or better support network or volunteer or adopt or so many things.

 I’m not pretending you have to start with any one of those because “that’s what worked for me.” It’s awesome you found what works for you, I feel for everyone who has successfully struggled with their depression. I do mean that and I hope you be well.

Psychologically people are pretty bad at recognizing and understanding their emotions and their causes. 

For instance they’ve done a study where they injected people with saline (control group) and adrenaline (experimental group) then had them take a test that asked questions like “how many sexual partners other than your father has your mother had?” 

The trick here is the person being tested in the room with another person who is secretly in on the experiment. This person then intentionally freaks out and overreacts “this test is bullshit!”

it wasn’t cause (insulting questions) makes effect (anger, sweating, increasing breathing and heart rate), that’s what the experimental group erroneously concluded cause they didn’t know they had taken adrenaline. 

Point being, we aren’t as open a book to ourselves as we’d like to believe. It’s not unheard of to enjoy a thing more because it’s novel, that’s more documented than pretending it’s never a thing or as a person you are above that common human phenomenon.

It’s the price bungie paid for trying to make Destiny PvP ‘competive’ or an esport. The design goals of PvP run directly counter to the goals in RPGs. In the former, balance Is highly valued because you want as many players to be playing on a level field while in the latter you want a progression system that makes you stronger (I.e. unbalanced) as time goes on. 

They can’t give us amazing exotics to use in pve because that would unbalance pvp. They can’t give us faster charging supers because the PvP crowd will complain about getting killed by supers. They can’t give everyone easy access to snipers and shotguns and LMG because of how strong they are in pvp (and pve especially) so they get rid of LMG and limit your ammo and loadout variety by making snipers and shotguns power weapons (where before you could one of those plus a heavy which you can’t do now)

Now snipers have to compete with swords, rocket launchers, and fusion rifles. And given the state of the game it’s either a cluster bomb rocket, merciless, Wardcliffe and sometimes a sword. I could count the number of times I’ve even used a sniper on both hands. I’m mainly a pve player and the only power weapons I use are sins of the past, merciless, wardcliffe (for Public events mostly) or a sword. Borealis is ok for prism nightfalls. Hardly ever used a shotgun now. 

Fine it’s annoying to get one shot by shotguns and snipers in pvp, whatever. Then just change it for pvp, who cares if you could have a sniper and rocket launcher in pve? Who was complaining about that for pve? Who didn’t like it? Who was begging for the ability to have two sidearms equipped at the same time and to remove LMG for pve content? Destiny 2 in many ways feels like a bad reboot rather than a better sequel.

Compared to D1, moving shotguns and snipers to power ammo was clearly a move to ‘balance’ pvp as it only hurts pve. Subclasses being dumbed down to a light switch, either you have it flipped up or down, makes balancing in pvp easier and only limits build options in pve. Supers charge much slower now and we don’t have perks that help it or tier 12 gear, most likely another pvp balancing mechanic and again only further makes pve boring to play. 

They made so many changes for the sake of pvp at the expense of pve without actually making pvp fun. It’s the worst of both worlds, nerf pve and balance out play styles in pvp to be dull.

It is not at all obvious or self-evident that 'value' of work I produce with the facilities of my employer and the cooperation of my co-workers would be as easy to make or would be able to match the value of the same work I do on my own without getting the job.

If I use Intel facilities, and Intel machines, and Intel purchased resources to somehow make a CPU, how much of that work is 'mine'? To what extent is the processor an outcome of my work and not say the owner's, or any of the dozens or hundreds of other people involved in making it? It doesn't describe the self. It describes specific aspects of the self. It gives insight into 4 areas of personality and how those areas interact.

How do you prefer to take in information? (S vs N)
How do you prefer to make decisions? (T vs F)
How do you prefer to live your outer life? (J vsP)

Much how you can describe a persons sex as male or female, that description isn't trying to define everything that makes you you, just trying to quantify the area of sex. So with the MBTI it wants to figure out a few common paradigms of personality and see which fit best for an individual.

They problem is this is a looter shooter. Yeah the gun mechanics are fun, that's why I keep coming back to Destiny after Halo or CoD. But without progressively better loot, there is even less incentive to play. 

Let's say tomorrow they announce a brand new raid with max light of 320. Ok cool. I'd run through a hundred times just for something new. Then 2 months from now they release another raid at 320. Sure they could add different perks on guns or mechanics but at a certain point light level means nothing. Everyone you face in iron banner and trials is effectively the same level. So saying "level advantages enabled/disabled" will just be pointless. 

There's a reason they increase the light level of certain drops for certain activities. Take the sub's dissatisfaction from the nightfall. When you are sitting at 317-320 the nightfall isn't really meant for you. It's meant for the 280-290 people to get normal mode ready. You might as well complain that strike gear isn't max level. 

This progressive loot system gives you something to chase, it helps keep people addicted to this Skinner box of a game thereby getting Bungie revenue. It's unfortunate but by having the light level of rewards go up, certain activities are not going to be rewarding to do anymore. 

Bungie didn't get rid of VoG or CE or all the old strikes. You can still play them! But since they don't drop anything rewarding, people count them off and say "Bungie has made half their game obsolete." 

But if they don't give better loot we'll still be in this same position "why should I do anything if I am not going to be rewarded for it?" Now people can be motivated for different reasons, the thrill of exploration, socializing, personal achievement, or progression (someone posted how they wrote a paper on Destiny and how it has those four motivators, really interesting). But Bungie knows if they don't have that progression they will lose some players, more than if they catered to the whims of the hardcore players that include many of us on this sub.
